benchmark package¶

Submodules¶

benchmark.benchmark module¶

Benchmark du produit matrice-vecteur : MatCooPure, MatCooOptim, numpy (dense) et scipy.

Deux expériences sont menées :

  • nnz : dimension fixe (la plus grande de DIMENSIONS), nombre d’éléments non nuls variable ;

  • dim : taux de remplissage fixe (DENSITE), dimension variable.

benchmark.benchmark.liste_nnz(N)[source]¶

Liste croissante de nombres d’éléments non nuls, terminée par N.

Exemples

>>> liste_nnz(1000)
[50, 100, 200, 500, 1000]
>>> liste_nnz(30)
[30]
benchmark.benchmark.operations(n, nnz, avec_pure=True)[source]¶

Construit une matrice aléatoire n x n avec nnz éléments et renvoie un dictionnaire {nom: fonction sans argument} calculant le produit matrice-vecteur.

Toutes les implémentations utilisent la même matrice et le même vecteur.

Exemples

>>> sorted(operations(10, 5, avec_pure=False))
['coo_optim', 'numpy', 'scipy']
benchmark.benchmark.rapport(res)[source]¶

Rapport textuel des résultats de run_benchmark() (temps en secondes).

benchmark.benchmark.run_benchmark(N=1000, avec_pure=True)[source]¶

Lance les deux expériences.

Paramètres:

  • N (int) – Nombre maximal d’éléments non nuls.

  • avec_pure (bool) – Inclure MatCooPure (lent) ou non.

Renvoie:

{"nnz": {"n": ..., "x": [...], "temps": {nom: [...]}}, "dim": {"x": [...], "nnz": [...], "temps": {nom: [...]}}} Un temps vaut nan si la mesure précédente a dépassé 1 s.

Type renvoyé:

dict

benchmark.benchmark.tracer(res, sortie='benchCOO.png')[source]¶

Trace les deux graphes côte à côte et les enregistre au format png dans sortie.

Product of two COO matrices, without Python loop.

class benchmark.mat_coo_pure.MatCooPure(n: int, m: int, data: List[Tuple[int, int, float]] = None)[source]¶

Bases : object

COO matrix class (see Wikipedia for more information).

Attributes:¶

The number of rows.

mint

The number of columns.

datalist of tuple

List containing a tuple of coordinates (i: int, j: int) and a float value.

nnzint

The number of non-zero elements (can be accessed but not modified).

dev_show()[source]¶

Displays a summary of the matrix and its memory footprint.

This method prints a summary of the matrix, including its size, the number of non-zero elements, the first two and last two non-zero elements (if they exist), and the memory footprint of the data.

Example:¶

>>> mat = MatCooPure(2, 2, [(0, 0, 1.0), (1, 1, 2.0)])
>>> mat.dev_show()
COO matrix ((2, 2)) with nnz=2
  0   0   1.00e+00
  1   1   2.00e+00
...
  0   0   1.00e+00
  1   1   2.00e+00

Memory footprint: 72 bytes.

benchmark.utils module¶

utils.py

This module provides utility functions for benchmarking and memory profiling.

Functions:¶

init_benchmark_results():

Returns a dictionary to store the benchmarking results for different matrix operations.

format_memory(mem_usage):

Takes a memory usage value in bytes and converts it to a more readable format (KB, MB, GB).

timer(operation, times, memories=None):

A timer function that measures the execution time and memory usage of a given operation.

print_benchmark_results(benchmark_results, sizes, show_memory_usage=True):

Prints the benchmarking results in human readable way.

plot_CPU_time_benchmark(sizes, benchmark_results, title=”Time Comparison”, xlabel=”Matrix Size”, ylabel=”Time (s)”):

Plots the CPU time benchmarking results.

benchmark.utils.format_memory(mem_usage)[source]¶
benchmark.utils.init_benchmark_results()[source]¶

Returns a dictionary with the following structure

benchmark.utils.plot_CPU_time_benchmark(sizes, benchmark_results, title='Time Comparison', xlabel='Matrix Size', ylabel='Time (s)', xlog=False, output=None)[source]¶
benchmark.utils.print_benchmark_results(benchmark_results, sizes, show_memory_usage=True)[source]¶
benchmark.utils.timer(operation: Callable, times: List, memories: List = None) → None[source]¶

An advanced timer. Note that for very fast operations, the timer’s overhead might be significant compared to the computation time. In such cases, feel free to retest using %timeit or modify the function.

Use case: memories = None: memory is not measured, avoiding unnecessary overhead. memories = []: memory is measured, and the results are stored in the memories list. => low computation times measured may not be representative of reality.

Arguments:¶

operation: the function to be called (without parentheses)

You can use a lambda function to pass arguments to the function. For example: lambda: my_function(arg1, arg2)

times: list

List in which computation times are stored. We add np.nan if the computation time exceeds 1 second.

memories: list or None

List in which used memory is stored. We add np.nan if the computation time exceeds 1 second. If None, memory is not measured.

Returns:¶

None

Exemple:¶

>>> times=[]
>>> timer(lambda : max([1, 20, 100]), times)
>>> print(times)
[1.6709964256733656e-06]
